Logan —

We pulled the requested artifacts and validated the APAC hosting posture. Summary below (I can produce the short PDF/pack by EOD UTC):

1) Hosting region: asia-southeast1 (primary) — no automatic cross-region failover enabled by default. Cross-region routing occurs only under documented disaster recovery runbooks and requires manual escalation.

2) Network diagram: attached as redwood_vpc_evidence_apac.pdf (diagram includes VPC ID vpc-0a1b2c3d, private-link endpoint pl-asia-017, subnet CIDRs for tenant isolation).

3) Routing manifest: routing_manifest_20261104.txt attached (lists VPC ID, subnets, endpoint IDs, peering entries and ACLs).

4) KMS/key isolation: We support customer-managed keys (HSM-backed) per-customer. Evidence: KMS partitioning statement included in SOC2 excerpt. Keys are scoped per-tenant and can be rotated independently; HSM-backed keys are available for Dedicated and Private customers.

5) Audit logs & retention: Audit logs are collected centrally and stored for 90 days by default in our logging cluster for hosted accounts; for Dedicated/Private we can extend retention per contract. Logs are accessible by audit export runbook (attached). Access to logs is via role-restricted service accounts; export requires JIRA ticket and approval from Infra Ops.

6) Sig/CAIQ notes: we've filled the CAIQ/partial SIG answers related to network segregation and data residency — see caiaq_responses_20261105.xlsx.

Deliverables attached: redwood_vpc_evidence_apac.pdf; routing_manifest_20261104.txt; soc2_snapshot_q3_2026.pdf (excerpt); caiaq_responses_20261105.xlsx; audit_export_runbook.txt.

If MediWell needs additional evidence (e.g., packet captures, longer retention windows), we can handle via a scoped evidence request and timeline.

Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
